intro: Art therapists read people closely and help them express what words cannot, skills that counseling and social work share. The closest of the 25 careers below is Marriage and Family Therapists, with an 89% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $66,940, and every option needs no more education than you have.
why_it_works: Sessions mean building trust, choosing creative activities and noticing what a client's work reveals. O*NET rates social perceptiveness at 4.25 out of 5 for this job, and service orientation and judgment at 3.88. Counseling, social work and college teaching use the same skills. BLS reports art therapists within a broader therapist group, so this page shows medians instead of percent changes.
tips: Marriage and family therapy is the closest licensed path; check how your hours transfer.
College art and design teaching is a 75% match with a median of $78,620.
Psychology Teachers, Postsecondary earn $80,340 and are a 73% match.

faq.q: What jobs can former art therapists do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Marriage and Family Therapists (89%), mental health and substance abuse social workers (84%) and Healthcare Social Workers (79%), based on O*NET 31.0. Rehabilitation Counselors are 78% matched, with a BLS May 2025 median of $46,850.

faq.q: Which jobs for art therapists pay the most?
faq.a: Among the 25 matches, the highest medians are postsecondary sociology teachers at $84,290, psychology teachers at $80,340 and philosophy and religion teachers at $80,260, according to BLS May 2025 data. College teaching often requires a doctorate in the subject, so check entry rules first.

faq.q: Do art therapists need another degree to switch?
faq.a: Not more education in general: all 25 matches need no more than art therapists already have. A master's degree is common, held by 77% of workers in a close match, but each counseling field has its own license requirements and supervised practice hours.

faq.q: What skills should art therapists build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are operations analysis, coordination, instructing and persuasion. Complex problem solving already rates 3.38 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so teaching and program skills are the main steps toward counseling and academic roles.
